content: California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is positioning the state to take the lead on AI oversight, including the potential to mandate a “kill switch” for frontier models, with a new executive order issued Friday.  Newsom’s order directs the state to convene a group of experts that will deliver recommendations within two months on how to strengthen AI safety measures in state law. Newsom wants the group to consider how the state could require AI companies to embed independent verification groups onsite for regular audits, make their transparency reports and risk assessments subject to standards of independent auditors, create a “kill switch” that’s routinely verified as effective, and make sure companies are required to report “loss-of-control incidents” like the OpenAI attack on Hugging Face as critical safety incidents. It also directs a state agency to speed up implementation of two recent laws he signed, creating a framework for independent verifiers to assess AI safety, and a state registry of AI auditors. There’s been a flurry of bill discussions in Congress in the wake of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s post warning of a more than 10 percent chance that AI “could kill all humans” within a decade. But there’s little hope in Washington that a bill of substance could pass anytime soon given that the House is on recess until November, and the impending midterm elections make major legislation movement in the Senate similarly unlikely. At the same time, President Donald Trump has insisted, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND ​SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Newsom’s executive order is likely not the last we’ll hear from California on this topic. On Wednesday, he floated the possibility of calling California lawmakers in for a special legislative session on AI in an interview with Politico, alongside potential executive action. He is specifically positioning the order as a model for federal action, calling on Congress and Trump “to review and adopt the state’s framework, or use its nation-leading regulation as a floor, not a ceiling, for the benefit and safety of all Americans.”  “The federal government’s abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation,” Newsom said in a statement. “We’re not waiting to act – we’re going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it’s too late. We’re going to do this thoughtfully but with urgent velocity; the stakes are too high to wait or delay action.”
chineseTitle: 加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 正在推动 AI 终止开关

chineseContent: 加州州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom，民主党) 周五发布了一项新的行政命令，该州将在人工智能监管方面发挥带头作用，包括有可能为前沿模型强制实施“终止开关”。  纽瑟姆的命令指示该州召集一个专家组，将在两个月内就如何加强州法律中的人工智能安全措施提出建议。纽瑟姆希望该小组考虑国家如何要求人工智能公司在现场嵌入独立核查小组进行定期审计，使其透明度报告和风险评估符合独立审计员的标准，创建一个定期验证有效的“终止开关”，并确保要求公司将像 OpenAI 对 Hugging Face 的攻击这样的“失控事件”作为重大安全事件进行报告。它还指示国家机构加快实施他最近签署的两项法律，为独立验证者评估人工智能安全建立框架，并建立人工智能审计员国家登记处。前人类学研究员雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 发帖警告称，人工智能在十年内“可能杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10%，此后，国会展开了一系列法案讨论。但鉴于众议院在 11 月之前休会，且即将举行的中期选举使得参议院同样不太可能采取重大立法行动，华盛顿方面不太可能很快通过实质法案。与此同时，唐纳德·特朗普总统坚称，“人工智能需要的唯一控制或‘护栏’是一位强大且聪明（高智商！）的总统，而美国确实拥有这样的总统！”纽瑟姆的行政命令可能不会是我们最后一次听到加州关于这个话题的行政命令。周三，他提出了致电卡利的可能性
